text:
Jake Guentzel spent part of this week back in Omaha, where Nebraska-Omaha retired his number at Baxter Arena. "It's just surreal," was how KETV's headline quoted him. Then it was back to the less sentimental work of being Tampa Bay's most reliable finisher.

He has 8 goals and 15 points in 15 games, and the underlying numbers back almost all of it. With him on the ice at five on five, the Lightning take 60.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 7.8 points better than when he sits. He is generating 1.23 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, right in line with last season's rate. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) says he lives in the home-plate area and on the end of royal-road passes, which is exactly where 30-goal seasons come from.

The caveat is modest: he is shooting 20% and the team is finishing a bit hot around him, and Evolving-Hockey notes his linemates flatter his raw numbers. Our range still puts him at about 37 goals. The jersey is in the rafters in Omaha; the work in Tampa looks unfinished.
headline: Guentzel keeps getting to the good ice
